subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Consider the following statements: I. Nitric acid is used in the production of fertilisers. II. 2,4-dichlorophenoxy acetic acid is a widely used weedicide. III. Sulphuric acid is used in Soda-acid fire extinguishers. Select the correct answer using the code given below:
solution: Nitric acid is consumed in making ammonium nitrate and other nitrogenous fertilisers, so I is true. 2,4-dichlorophenoxyacetic acid (2,4-D) is a standard selective weedicide, so II is true. The soda-acid fire extinguisher works by tipping sulphuric acid into sodium bicarbonate solution to generate carbon dioxide, so III is true. Matches option D.

stem: On passing carbon dioxide gas through water, the white immiscible compound formed is:
solution: Carbon dioxide passed through lime water gives a white insoluble precipitate of calcium carbonate, \(\text{Ca(OH)}_{2} + \text{CO}_{2} \to \text{CaCO}_{3} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}\), which is the test for carbon dioxide. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Stem defect preserved as printed: carbon dioxide passed through plain WATER gives soluble carbonic acid, not a white solid. The white insoluble calcium carbonate the question describes forms with LIME WATER. Printed key (a) is the intended answer and is retained; 'immiscible' should also read 'insoluble'.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Mixing an acid or base with water results in ________ in the concentration of ions (\(\text{H}_{3}\text{O}^{+}/\text{OH}^{-}\)) per unit volume
optD: Decrease at first and then spike after sometime
solution: Adding water spreads the same number of ions through a larger volume, so the number of hydronium or hydroxide ions per unit volume falls. This is dilution, and it is why dilution must be done by adding acid to water. Matches option C.
reviewNote: Semantic DUP of bank row 16feaac6-4c7b-47a0-b84a-034a2c11b91b (dedup pass, option-verified). Kept in the paper + OMR sheet for Q-number parity; must stay PRIVATE if this paper is ever committed.

stem: Which of the following can react with an Acid?
solution: Sodium carbonate is the salt of a weak acid and reacts with any acid to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide. Silver chloride and lead sulphate are insoluble and unreactive towards dilute acid, and sodium sulphate is the salt of a strong acid and a strong base, so none of them reacts. Matches option B.

stem: Setting of Plaster of Paris takes place due to:
solution: Plaster of Paris, \(\text{CaSO}_{4}\cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\), takes up water to become gypsum, \(\text{CaSO}_{4}\cdot 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\), and sets into a hard mass. Water is added, not removed, so the change is hydration. Matches option D.

stem: Which one among the following is not a property of salt?
optA: Salts have ordered packing arrangements called lattices.
optB: Salts have low melting but high boiling points
optD: Salts conduct electricity when dissolved in water or even in the molten state
solution: Salts are ionic solids held by strong electrostatic forces, so they have both high melting points and high boiling points. The statement that they melt at low temperature is therefore not a property of salts, while the ordered lattice, brittleness and conduction in solution or melt all are. Matches option B.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Consider the following statements: I. Metal ions are Lewis Acids. II. Metal ions are electron pair acceptors.
optA: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is correct explanation of statement I.
optB: Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not correct explanation of statement I.
optC: Statement I is true but statement II is false.
optD: Statement I is false but statement II is true.
solution: A Lewis acid is defined as an electron pair acceptor. A metal ion has vacant orbitals and a positive charge, so it accepts an electron pair from a ligand, and that is precisely why it behaves as a Lewis acid. Statement II is therefore the correct explanation of statement I. Matches option A.

stem: Which one among the following is not a double salt?
solution: A double salt is made of two simple salts that crystallise together and dissociate completely into all their ions in solution, such as potash alum, Mohr's salt and chrome alum. Sodium chloride is a simple normal salt of one acid and one base. Matches option D.

stem:
Match List-1 and List-2 and select the correct code:

| List 1 (Name of Salt) | List 2 (Formula) |
|---|---|
| A. Blue vitriol | 1. \(\text{K}_{2}\text{SO}_{4}\cdot \text{Al}_{2}(\text{SO}_{4})_{3}\cdot 24\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\) |
| B. Mohr's salt | 2. \(\text{CaOCl}_{2}\) |
| C. Bleaching powder | 3. \((\text{NH}_{4})_{2}\text{Fe}(\text{SO}_{4})_{2}\cdot 6\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\) |
| D. Potash alum | 4. \(\text{CuSO}_{4}\cdot 5\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\) |
solution: Blue vitriol is copper sulphate pentahydrate, so A pairs with 4. Mohr's salt is ammonium iron(II) sulphate hexahydrate, so B pairs with 3. Bleaching powder is calcium oxychloride, so C pairs with 2. Potash alum is potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate written with 24 waters, so D pairs with 1. Matches option C.
reviewNote: KEY FLIP vs printed key (a -> C). Printed (a) maps Mohr's salt to CaOCl2 and bleaching powder to (NH4)2Fe(SO4)2.6H2O, which is chemically impossible. Correct pairing A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1 is option (c).

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which of the following materials can be used by a visually impaired person as an acid-base indicator?
solution: A visually impaired person cannot read a colour change, so the indicator must act on another sense. Vanilla essence is an olfactory indicator whose characteristic smell is destroyed in a basic solution, while litmus, turmeric and petunia petals all signal by colour. Matches option C.

stem: Sodium Carbonate is a basic salt because it is a salt of:
solution: Sodium carbonate is formed from carbonic acid, which is weak, and sodium hydroxide, which is strong. The anion of the weak acid hydrolyses in water to release hydroxide ions, making the solution basic. Matches option D.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which of the following phenomena occur, when a small amount of acid is added to water?
solution: Adding an acid to water is exothermic, but the change that actually takes place is that the acid dissociates and produces hydronium ions in solution. No base is present, so there is no neutralisation, and nothing insoluble separates out. Matches option C.

subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Consider the following statements about HCl gas: I. On passing through water, it ionises the solution. II. It turns the dry blue litmus red. III. It forms hydronium ion when passed through water.
solution: Statement I is true because hydrogen chloride dissolves and ionises in water. Statement III is true because the proton released is taken up by water as the hydronium ion. Statement II is false: dry hydrogen chloride gas has no free hydrogen ions and leaves dry blue litmus unchanged, which is the standard demonstration that acidic behaviour needs water. Matches option D.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: How does the dock plant help in relieving the pain caused by nettle sting?
optB: It neutralises the acid with the base
optC: It neutralises the base with another base
optD: It dilutes the acid by adding water content to the affected area.
solution: A nettle sting injects methanoic acid into the skin. The dock leaf that grows near the nettle is basic, so rubbing it on the sting neutralises that acid and relieves the pain. Matches option B.
reviewNote: KEY FLIP vs printed key (c -> B). A nettle sting injects an ACID, so the basic dock leaf neutralises the acid with a base, i.e. option (b). Printed option (c) reads 'neutralises the base with another base', which is not neutralisation at all.

stem: The substances with pH less than 7 are: 1. Gastric juices 2. Coffee 3. Apple juice 4. Liquid in car battery
solution: Gastric juice, coffee, apple juice and the sulphuric acid in a car battery are all acidic, so every one of them has a pH below 7. Matches option D.

subtopic: Common Acids: Names, Formulas and Uses
stem: Which of the following is not a mineral acid?
solution: Mineral acids are the inorganic acids made from mineral sources, such as perchloric, hydrochloric and sulphuric acid. Acetic acid is a carboxylic acid obtained from an organic source, so it is an organic acid. Matches option B.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Non-metallic oxides react with base to form:
solution: Oxides of non-metals are acidic, and an acidic oxide neutralises a base to give a salt and water, as in \(\text{CO}_{2} + 2\text{NaOH} \to \text{Na}_{2}\text{CO}_{3} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}\). No hydrogen is released because no metal is involved. Matches option B.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which of the following is incorrect?
optA: Bases are bitter in taste and soapy in touch.
optC: Alkali is a base that dissolves in water.
optD: All the metallic oxides are either basic or amphoteric.
solution: Only those bases that dissolve in water are called alkalis; many bases such as copper hydroxide and iron(III) hydroxide are insoluble. So the claim that all bases dissolve in water is the incorrect statement, while the bitter taste, the soapy feel and the definition of an alkali are all correct. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Option (d) is also strictly false at higher level (Mn2O7 and CrO3 are acidic metal oxides), but at NCERT scope it reads true and (b) is unambiguously the intended and correct answer.

stem: Washing soda is used in the manufacture of:
solution: Washing soda is a source of sodium for other sodium compounds, and it is used in the manufacture of borax. Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime, and gypsum and calcium carbonate are calcium compounds, so none of them uses washing soda. Matches option C.
reviewNote: KEY FLIP vs printed key (d -> C). NCERT states washing soda is used in the manufacture of borax. Bleaching powder is made from chlorine and dry slaked lime, which uses no washing soda.

stem: What happens to gypsum when heated at 373 K?
optA: Loses water molecules and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate.
optB: Gains water molecules and becomes calcium chloride decahydrate.
optC: It burns and the ash is calcium sulphate.
optD: It turns into anhydrous calcium sulphate also called dead burnt plaster.
solution: On heating to 373 K gypsum, \(\text{CaSO}_{4}\cdot 2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\), loses three quarters of its water of crystallisation and becomes calcium sulphate hemihydrate, \(\text{CaSO}_{4}\cdot \tfrac{1}{2}\text{H}_{2}\text{O}\), which is Plaster of Paris. Dead burnt plaster forms only on much stronger heating. Matches option A.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Consider the statements regarding the process of oxidation of alcohol: 1. Esters is formed as one of the major products. 2. Acidified \(\text{K}_{2}\text{Cr}_{2}\text{O}_{7}\) is used as an oxidising agent. 3. Heat is not involved in this reaction. Correct code:
solution: Alcohols are oxidised to carboxylic acids, not esters, so statement 1 is false. Acidified potassium dichromate is the standard oxidising agent, so statement 2 is true. The reaction is carried out on warming, so statement 3 is false. Matches option C.

stem: Saturated hydrocarbons generally burn with a:
solution: Saturated hydrocarbons have a low proportion of carbon and burn completely in air, giving a clean blue flame. A yellow sooty flame comes from unsaturated hydrocarbons, whose unburnt carbon glows. Matches option B.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Denatured alcohol is made by adding poisonous substances like ______ to prevent misuse.
solution: Denaturing means making ethanol unfit to drink without affecting its industrial use. Methanol is added for this purpose because it is poisonous. Matches option C.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: In the nomenclature of organic compounds, a three-carbon chain with a ketone group is named:
solution: A three carbon chain gives the root prop, the saturated chain gives an, and the ketone group gives the suffix one, so the compound is propanone. Propanal is the aldehyde, propanol the alcohol and propanoic acid the carboxylic acid. Matches option C.

stem: Consider the following regarding aromatic compounds: 1. Their stability is due to high resonance energy. 2. They should be non-cyclic in nature. 3. They should always be non-planar. Select the incorrect answer using the code given below:
solution: Aromatic compounds are stabilised by a large resonance energy, so statement 1 is correct. But they must be cyclic and they must be planar for the ring to delocalise its electrons, so statements 2 and 3 are wrong. The question asks for the incorrect ones. Matches option B.

stem: Consider the following statements regarding the permanent hardness of water: 1. Washing soda treatment 2. Ion exchange method 3. Reverse Osmosis 4. Clark's method (lime treatment) How many of the above methods can be used for the removal of permanent hardness of water?
solution: Permanent hardness is due to chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, and it is removed by washing soda, by ion exchange and by reverse osmosis. Clark's lime method removes only temporary hardness, which is caused by bicarbonates. Three methods therefore work. Matches option C.

stem: Which one of the following characteristics is possessed by enantiomers?
solution: Enantiomers are non superimposable mirror images with identical physical properties, so their melting points, solubilities and refractive indices are the same. They differ only in the direction in which they rotate plane polarised light. Matches option C.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Arrange the following compounds in their ascending order of boiling point:
solution: Methane is a small non polar gas and boils lowest. Chloroform is polar but cannot hydrogen bond. Ethanol hydrogen bonds, and acetic acid hydrogen bonds as a dimer, so it boils highest. The order is methane, chloroform, ethanol, acetic acid. Matches option A.

stem: Consider the following statements: 1. Acetylene has one triple bond between 2 carbon atoms. 2. Ethene has one double bond between 3 carbon atoms. 3. Formaldehyde is an aldehyde. Correct code:
solution: Acetylene has a triple bond between its two carbon atoms, so statement 1 is true. Ethene has only two carbon atoms, so a double bond between three carbons is impossible and statement 2 is false. Formaldehyde carries the CHO group and is the simplest aldehyde, so statement 3 is true. Matches option C.

subtopic: Mole Concept, Avogadro's Law and Molar Calculations
stem: A solution is prepared by adding 2 g of a substance A to 18 g of water. Calculate the mass per cent of the solute.
solution: Mass per cent of solute is the mass of solute divided by the mass of the whole solution. The solution weighs \(2 + 18 = 20\) g, so the mass per cent is \((2/20)\times 100 = 10\%\). Dividing by the mass of water alone gives the wrong value 11.11 per cent. Matches option A.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Consider the following statements regarding the dehydration reaction of alcohols: 1. Alcohol produces alkyne as the final product. 2. Water molecules are also formed as an end product. Correct code:
solution: Dehydration of an alcohol removes a molecule of water and gives an alkene, not an alkyne, so statement 1 is false. Water is the other product, so statement 2 is true. Matches option B.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Muskan was demonstrating an experiment with a gas X. She took a very small piece of sodium and dropped it into a test tube containing ethanol (absolute alcohol). She observed bubbles of gas emerging out. With regard to this experiment, mark the correct statement:
optA: When a burning matchstick is brought near the mouth of the test tube, it instantly extinguishes.
optB: The gas has a pungent odour.
optC: Dark white fumes appeared on the walls of the test tube.
optD: The gas is odourless, colourless, but burns with a popping sound when a burning matchstick is brought near the mouth of the test tube.
solution: Sodium reacts with ethanol to give sodium ethoxide and hydrogen gas. Hydrogen is colourless and odourless and burns with a characteristic pop when a lighted splint is brought to the mouth of the tube. Matches option D.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Consider the statements regarding esterification: 1. Ethanoic acid and ethanol react together to form esters. 2. On treatment with sodium hydroxide, which is an alkali, the ester is converted back to alcohol and sodium salt of carboxylic acid. 3. An acid is used as a catalyst in this reaction. Correct code:
solution: Ethanoic acid and ethanol give an ester, so statement 1 is true. Warming the ester with sodium hydroxide is saponification and returns the alcohol and the sodium salt of the acid, so statement 2 is true. Concentrated sulphuric acid is the catalyst, so statement 3 is true. Matches option D.

subtopic: Functional Groups and Common Organic Compounds
stem: Consider the following regarding carboxylic acid: 1. In carboxylic acid, carbon (C) atom is bonded to an oxygen (O) atom by a double bond and to a hydroxyl group (—OH) by a single bond. 2. Carboxylic acids have lower boiling points than ketones, alcohols and aldehydes. Correct code:
solution: The carboxyl group has the carbon doubly bonded to one oxygen and singly bonded to a hydroxyl group, so statement 1 is true. Carboxylic acids form hydrogen bonded dimers and therefore boil higher, not lower, than comparable alcohols, aldehydes and ketones, so statement 2 is false. Matches option A.

stem: What is the amount of Carbon dioxide present in the earth's atmosphere?
solution: Carbon dioxide makes up about 0.03 per cent of the atmosphere by volume. Nitrogen and oxygen account for about 78 and 21 per cent respectively. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following hydrocarbons contains 25% Hydrogen by mass? (Hydrogen = 1, C = 12)
solution: Compute the hydrogen fraction for each. Methane has mass \(12 + 4 = 16\) with 4 units of hydrogen, giving \(4/16 = 25\%\). Ethene gives \(4/28 = 14.3\%\), propane \(8/44 = 18.2\%\) and ethyne \(2/26 = 7.7\%\). Matches option B.

stem: Which chemical bond is formed between two copper atoms? 1. Covalent bond 2. Ionic bond 3. Coordinate covalent bond 4. Metallic bond Select the correct answer:
solution: Copper is a metal, and a bond between two identical metal atoms is formed by their valence electrons being delocalised over a lattice of positive ions. That is a metallic bond. Matches option D.

subtopic: Atomic Number, Mass Number and Subatomic Particles
stem: Consider the points regarding neutrinos: 1. Electrically neutral subatomic particles. 2. Negative electric charge. 3. Very small mass. Correct code:
solution: Neutrinos carry no electric charge, so statement 1 is true and statement 2 is false. Their mass is extremely small but not zero, so statement 3 is true. Matches option C.

stem: Which of the following is correct about the first ionization enthalpy of alkaline earth metals?
optA: It is higher than corresponding Group 1 metals
optB: It is lower than corresponding Group 1 metals
solution: Across a period the nuclear charge rises and the atomic size falls, so a Group 2 atom holds its outer electron more tightly than the Group 1 atom in the same period. The first ionisation enthalpy of an alkaline earth metal is therefore higher. Matches option A.

stem: Villagers in some parts of India use the water extract of the ash obtained by burning banana plants as a substitute of soda. Which one of the following is the major active component in the extract?
solution: Banana plants take up large amounts of potassium, so the ash left on burning them is rich in potassium salts. Its water extract contains mainly potassium carbonate, which is why it behaves like soda. Matches option B.

stem: Which one among the following is not an ore of copper?
solution: Chalcopyrite, cuprite and chalcocite are naturally occurring copper minerals from which the metal is extracted. Copper sulphate is a manufactured salt, not a mineral deposit, so it is not an ore. Matches option D.

stem: Consider the following statements in reference to the process of Roasting: 1. In roasting, the ore is heated in a regular supply of air in a furnace at a temperature below the melting point of the metal. 2. Roasting is done for carbonate ores. 3. Ores of copper are usually reduced through the roasting process. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Roasting heats the ore in a plentiful supply of air below the melting point of the metal, so statement 1 is true. It is used for sulphide ores, while carbonate ores are calcined, so statement 2 is false. Copper occurs mainly as sulphide ores and is treated by roasting, so statement 3 is true. Matches option C.

subtopic: Acid-Base Theory: Concepts, Oxides and Electrolytes
stem: Which among the following will neither react with a base nor an acid?
solution: Carbon monoxide and nitric oxide are neutral oxides and react with neither acids nor bases. Aluminium oxide and zinc oxide are amphoteric and react with both. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Near-duplicate check: 94f12fff-7957-4fe2-9e0d-d231d3aaf0b6 asks the same neutral-oxide fact but as a single-oxide question; this one pairs oxides, so it stands as separate.

stem: Which among the following does not have copper as one of its constituents?
solution: Bronze is copper with tin and brass is copper with zinc, so both contain copper. Duralumin is an aluminium alloy that also carries about four per cent copper along with magnesium and manganese. Solder is an alloy of lead and tin only, so it is the one with no copper. Matches option D.
reviewNote: KEY FLIP vs printed key (c -> D). Duralumin contains about 4 per cent copper, so it is NOT copper-free. Solder is lead and tin only, so option (d) is the only alloy here without copper.

stem: Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List-I (Element) List-II (Property/Use) 1 Ag a Overhead power transmission lines 2 Hg b Electrode in dry cells and batteries 3 Zn c Amalgam for filling teeth 4 Al d Printed circuit boards
solution: Silver is the best conductor and is used in printed circuit boards, so 1 pairs with d. Mercury forms the amalgam used for dental fillings, so 2 pairs with c. Zinc is the electrode in dry cells, so 3 pairs with b. Aluminium is light and is used for overhead transmission lines, so 4 pairs with a. Matches option B.

subtopic: Reactivity Series and Reactions with Water
stem: Reaction between which of the following two reactants will produce hydrogen gas?
solution: Magnesium lies above hydrogen in the reactivity series and displaces it from hydrochloric acid to give hydrogen gas. Nitric acid is a strong oxidising agent and oxidises the hydrogen to water, so copper and zinc with nitric acid give oxides of nitrogen instead. Calcium carbonate with acid gives carbon dioxide. Matches option A.
reviewNote: Near-duplicate check: 28bad89b-5eec-40bf-b1e2-753c3ac32d1a is the inverse framing (which does NOT evolve hydrogen) over an overlapping reactant pool; option pairs differ, so kept as new.

subtopic: Reactivity Series and Reactions with Water
stem: Which among the following group of metal oxides are soluble in water?
solution: Oxides of the alkali metals are strongly basic and dissolve in water to give the corresponding hydroxides, so sodium oxide and potassium oxide are soluble. Zinc, magnesium, aluminium and beryllium oxides are insoluble in water. Matches option B.
reviewNote: Option (d) is printed as 'LiO', which is not a valid formula (lithium oxide is Li2O). Preserved as printed; it is a distractor and does not affect the key. Near-duplicate check: f7d03031-4a83-485a-bf84-ec9536115e5b asks for a SINGLE water-soluble oxide; this one asks for a GROUP, so kept as new.

stem: Consider the following statements in reference to anodizing: 1. It is the process of forming a thick oxide layer of aluminium. 2. A clean aluminium article is made the cathode. 3. The oxygen gas evolves at the anode. Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution: Anodising builds a thick protective oxide film on aluminium, so statement 1 is true. The article is made the anode, which is what the name means, so statement 2 is false. Oxygen is liberated at the anode and it is this oxygen that thickens the film, so statement 3 is true. Matches option C.

subtopic: Reactivity Series and Reactions with Water
stem: Which among the following is the correct order of elements in decreasing order of the reactive series?
solution: In the reactivity series zinc is above iron, iron is above lead and lead is above copper. The decreasing order is therefore zinc, iron, lead, copper. Matches option D.
reviewNote: Near-duplicate check: e1776ca5-baf3-4c97-be0a-8be0303f3f6e shares the framing but over a different element set (bank Na/Fe/Cu/Ag vs Fe/Zn/Pb/Cu here), so kept as new.

stem: Cinnabar is reduced to mercury by:
solution: Mercury is very low in the reactivity series, so its sulphide ore needs no separate reducing agent. Cinnabar is roasted in air, which converts it to mercuric oxide and then liberates the metal, and the mercury distils off. Matches option B.
reviewNote: PRINTED KEY RETAINED (b) but contestable. Strictly the reduction step HgO -> Hg happens on further heating alone, which is option (c); NCERT's own wording is 'reduced to mercury on further heating'. Roasting is defensible as the single process applied to cinnabar (self-reduction). Confirm with the setter before grading.
